rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests a balanced multimodal configuration (scvi_n200 RNA + resnet50 image) with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion. It clarifies the effectiveness of multimodal processing for multiprofile data while keeping costs low (resnet50 is cheaper than imagenet_vit_l, avgpool is less expensive than transformer). This is the best use of the first experiment to establish a baseline for multimodal approaches.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves 0.6776 validation accuracy. This experiment tests switching to transformer aggregation (more complex feature interaction) while retaining weighted fusion (proven effective in config_001). This clarifies whether transformer aggregation improves performance without changing the fusion strategy. It's a logical extension of the multimodal approach with similar cost (estimated ~6.5 GPU hours) and balances exploration of aggregation methods with exploitation of existing fusion effectiveness.

The existing evidence shows config_022 (multimodal, multiprofile, resnet50, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests upgrading the image encoder to imagenet_vit_l (a larger, more complex model) while keeping the same aggregation and fusion strategy. This clarifies whether the image encoder's capacity is a key factor in performance. The expected cost is higher than config_022 (approx 7-8 GPU hours), but it's a logical extension of the current best configuration, balancing exploitation of promising components with exploration of model complexity.

The existing evidence shows config_041 (0.7249 accuracy) is the best so far with low cost (3.60 GPU hours). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion, which could improve accuracy by leveraging a more expressive RNA encoder while maintaining the effective image encoder and fusion method from config_041. The expected cost is moderate (similar to config_041's image encoder complexity) and balances exploration of RNA encoder variations with exploitation of proven components.

The existing evidence shows config_041 (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.7249). This experiment tests changing the fusion method to 'concat' while keeping the effective RNA/image encoders (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l) and transformer aggregation. This clarifies if fusion method variation impacts performance. Expected cost is similar to config_041 (3.60 GPU hours), providing a low-cost way to explore a promising architectural direction without sacrificing efficiency.

The existing evidence shows config_041 (0.7249 accuracy) is the best so far using scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. This experiment tests pca_n2000 RNA with the same image encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion. It clarifies whether RNA encoder choice or fusion method is critical. Expected cost is similar to config_041 (3.60 GPU hours), balancing exploration of RNA encoder variations while maintaining low cost.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_041) achieves the highest accuracy (0.724989). This experiment tests avgpool aggregation and concat fusion with the same RNA/image encoders to compare aggregation methods and fusion strategies. It clarifies if simpler aggregation/fusion could maintain high accuracy while reducing cost. Expected cost is ~3.0 GPU hours, balancing exploration of aggregation methods with budget constraints.

Existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoders with transformer aggregation (config_041) achieve the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests avgpool aggregation with weighted fusion, a simpler alternative, to determine if it can match performance while reducing training cost. It clarifies whether aggregation method impacts accuracy and balances exploration of cheaper configurations against the current best.

The existing evidence shows config_041 (0.725 accuracy) is the top performer, but config_046 uses scgpt (potentially better RNA encoder) and transformer aggregation (used in top configs) with resnet50 (cost-effective image encoder). This experiment tests if combining scgpt with transformer fusion could surpass config_041's accuracy while maintaining manageable cost (estimated ~4.5 GPU hours). It balances exploration of RNA encoder improvements with cost efficiency.

The existing evidence shows config_041 (0.724989 accuracy) is the top performer with scvi_n200 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoders. This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with the same image encoder and transformer aggregation/weighted fusion, which could potentially improve accuracy while maintaining similar cost. The expected cost is moderate (similar to config_041's 3.60 GPU hours) and this configuration clarifies if RNA encoder choice significantly impacts performance with the same image encoder.
